title: Architect of the Infinite Dungeon
author: Marcus Vance
synopsis: When Earth's orbital ring collapses into the System Integration event, structural engineer Kai Mercer doesn't receive a combat class—he receives [Grand Architect — Unique]. Instead of swinging a sword, he designs physics-defying labyrinth floors, automated mana turbines, and impenetrable strongholds that turn humanity's last safe zone into an unstoppable fortress.

glossary.desc: Allows structural blueprints to materialize using raw Mana Concrete and Aether Blueprints.
Measures ambient magical concentration; above 4.0 MDI, steel alloys gain arcane conductivity.

reviews.text: Finally a LitRPG where engineering math and load-bearing trusses actually matter! The trap rooms are pure genius.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Load-Bearing Mana
chapters.authorNoteTop: Stats and system boxes are cleanly formatted for easy mobile reading!
chapters.content:
The sky over Sector 9 cracked like tempered glass at 08:14 AM, right as Kai was arguing with a contractor about reinforced concrete tolerances.

Ten seconds later, the contractor was staring at a glowing bronze sword hovering above his clipboard, while Kai stood beneath a swirling wireframe hologram of a geodesic dome.

[SYSTEM INTEGRATION COMPLETE — SECTOR 9]
[Class Assigned: Grand Architect (Unique — Tier 0)]
[Passive Skill Unlocked: Structural Sight Lv. 1]
[Warning: First Rift Tide arrives in 01:44:59]

All around the half-finished subway atrium, glowing blue stress lines blossomed across every pillar, rebar beam, and cracked slab of asphalt. Kai blinked. He could literally *see* shear force pulsing in crimson along the east retaining wall—and worse, he could see a jagged violet tear widening above the street entrance, leaking cold ozone and the distant chittering of armored carapace.

"Hey! Mercer!" yelled Elena, the site safety lead, clutching a glowing silver buckler that had just manifested over her high-vis vest. "The street barricade won't hold whatever's coming out of that purple hole. Do you have a combat skill?"

Kai lifted his right hand. A translucent blue drafting grid snapped neatly over the subway entrance, snapping to the existing steel I-beams with satisfying geometric clicks.

"No," Kai said, dragging a virtual wall forty feet across the tunnel mouth and watching his Mana bar tick downward. "I have something better. Tell everyone to get behind the yellow line—I'm turning this subway station into a kill-box with proper drainage."

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The First Funnel
chapters.authorNoteBottom: What trap should Kai build on Floor 2?
chapters.content:
Most people treated dungeons as dark caves stuffed with monsters. Kai treated them like hydraulic engineering problems.

If forty-two chitinous Rift-Stalkers poured through a thirty-foot archway simultaneously, twenty terrified civilians with starter spears would be overwhelmed in twelve seconds flat. Narrow that same thirty-foot archway into a zigzagging six-foot chevron corridor lined with waist-high firing slits and slick basalt flooring, however, and suddenly the monsters had to queue politely like commuters during rush hour.

[Blueprint Confirmed: Bastion Chevron Mk. I]
[Materials Consumed: 18 Tons Rubble, 240 Mana]
[Construction Time: 14 Seconds]

Broken concrete lifted off the shattered boulevard in a roaring spiral, fusing seamlessly with glowing veins of blue mana-mortar. Within fourteen seconds, twin angled walls of seamless obsidian-grey composite sealed the subway ramp, leaving only a winding S-curve throat flanked by elevated archer walkways.

Elena stared up at the smooth, mathematically perfect crenellations. "You built a medieval star-fort out of an old parking garage."

"Vauban's principles hold up even with magic," Kai replied, already sketching a pressure-plate counterweight directly over the choke point. "Now hand me those steel pipes—we have forty minutes before the wave hits, and I want gravity doing at least sixty percent of our DPS."
